overview.headline: Genes as DNA units that code proteins and shape variation

keyPoints.point: A gene functions as the basic unit of heredity and is made of DNA.
keyPoints.quote: A gene is the basic physical and functional unit of heredity.

keyPoints.point: Many genes do not code for proteins and instead help control other genes.
keyPoints.quote: However, many genes do not code for proteins, instead they help control other genes.

keyPoints.point: Human genes vary in size and the human genome now contains about 19,900 genes that produce proteins.
keyPoints.quote: We now know that the human genome contains about 19,900 genes used to produce proteins.

keyPoints.point: Different alleles are forms of the same gene with small differences in DNA sequence.
keyPoints.quote: Forms of the same gene with small differences in their sequence of DNA bases are called alleles.

keyPoints.point: People typically inherit two copies of each gene, one copy from each parent.
keyPoints.quote: Typically, people have two copies of each gene, one inherited from each parent.
